predecessors.name: Saadi Sultanate
predecessors.text: Marrakesh and the south, captured in July 1668

predecessors.name: Dila'iya Sultanate
predecessors.text: Fez (surrendered June 1666) and the Dila'iya domain in the north and the Middle Atlas (destroyed June 1668)

ledger.x: 1631: Mawlay al-Sharif is recognised as sultan of the Tafilalt and the Alawi (Alaouite) state begins.
June 1666: Fez becomes the Alawi capital ('made it his capital').
June 1666: al-Rashid takes Fez.
June 1668: al-Rashid destroys the Dala'iyya capital in the Middle Atlas.
July 1668: al-Rashid captures Marrakesh and the Alawis hold all Morocco.
1672: Moulay Isma'il, who reigned 1672-1727, moves the capital from Fez to Meknes.
7 February 1684: Morocco takes Tangier.
1769: Portugal abandons Mazagan and Sultan Mohammed ben Abdallah takes it over.
19 June 1844: Bugeaud occupies Oujda.
18 March 1845: the Treaty of Lalla Maghnia fixes the frontier.
1848: Spain conquers the Chafarinas Islands off the Mediterranean coast.
December 1859: the Spanish army opens the Tetouan campaign.
26 April 1860: the Treaty of Wad-Ras (the Peace of Tetouan) ends the war.
26 April 1860: Morocco cedes Santa Cruz de la Mar Pequena to Spain for a fishing post.
1912: Tangier is excluded from the protectorates.
30 March 1912: the Treaty of Fez makes Morocco a French protectorate.
27 November 1912: the Spanish protectorate in northern Morocco and the Cape Juby strip.
2 March 1956: France recognises Morocco's independence.
7 April 1956: Spain retrocedes the northern zone.
29 October 1956: Tangier rejoins Morocco.
1957: Mohammed V adopts the title of king and the sultanate becomes the Kingdom of Morocco.
1 April 1958: Spain cedes the Tarfaya strip (Cape Juby).
5 January 1969: Spain hands Ifni back.
6 November 1975: the Green March.
1976: Spain leaves and Morocco and Mauritania annex the territory.
27 February 1976: the Polisario proclaims the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic at Bir Lehlu and Morocco holds most of the territory.

wars.name: Siege of Tangier (1678-1680)
wars.outcome: The siege 'between 1678 and 1680' failed; the English garrison destroyed the town and port and left, and Morocco occupied Tangier on 7 February 1684.

wars.name: Franco-Moroccan War
wars.outcome: France won at Isly on 14 August 1844; the Treaty of Tangier (10 September 1844) ended the war and the Treaty of Lalla Maghnia (18 March 1845) drew the frontier from the Mediterranean to Teniet el-Sassi, leaving the south of Figuig undefined.

wars.name: Hispano-Moroccan War (1859-1860)
wars.outcome: Spain entered Tetouan on 6 February 1860; the Treaty of Wad-Ras (26 April 1860) gave Spain Santa Cruz de la Mar Pequena (Ifni), recognised Spanish Ceuta, Melilla and the Chafarinas, and set an indemnity of 20,000,000 duros.

wars.name: Rif War
wars.outcome: The Rif Republic (1921-1926) 'was subdued by a joint Spanish and French expedition'.

wars.name: Ifni War
wars.outcome: Morocco 'gained Tarfaya in the Ifni War'; the cession is dated by the Treaty of Angra de Cintra, 1 April 1958.

wars.name: Sand War
wars.outcome: 'The Sand War was fought between Algerian and Moroccan troops' in 1963; the page gives no territorial result, so no zone and no contest event.

wars.name: Western Sahara War
wars.outcome: Morocco and Mauritania annexed the territory in 1976; the SADR was proclaimed on 27 February 1976; Mauritania withdrew in 1979; the sand wall was built 1980-1987; a ceasefire came in 1991 and sovereignty is unresolved, the Polisario holding about 30 percent.

certainty.note: No treaty frontiers are on the pages: the Atlas, the Draa and the Saharan edge are approximate; Tangier and Mazagan, the Spanish and Portuguese places, are points.
The Algerian frontier from the Mediterranean to Teniet el-Sassi is sharp from the 18 March 1845 treaty; south of Figuig it is undefined.
Treaty zones: the French protectorate of 30 March 1912, the Spanish protectorate of 27 November 1912 and the Tangier zone; the state itself has no drawn shape.
The Mediterranean enclaves and the Tangier and Spanish-zone limits are sharp; the Algerian frontier south of Figuig (Sand War 1963) and the Western Sahara line along the sand wall are not settled.
